answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make new identities earn trust through time-locked reputation: each agent must complete a long sequence of verifiable tasks before earning full rights, like a tundra expedition advancing one camp at a time. Rewards vest slowly, so a flood of fresh identities earns almost nothing while honest agents compound credibility. If an agent cheats, its reputation collapses in a downward spiral and all vested rewards are slashed at once. Mass identity creation is uneconomic: each fake pays the full cost of a slow, basalt-hard climb, yet loses everything in one fraud.
